items.example: Working this weekend? It's not ideal, but fine.
items.exampleTr: Bu hafta sonu çalışmak mı? İdeal sayılmaz ama olur.
items.simple: A soft way to say something is bad or annoying.
dialogue: A: They've moved the meeting to 8 a.m. on Friday.
B: Hmm. It's not ideal, but I'll be there.
items.note: İngilizler 'berbat' yerine böyle der; kötüyü hafifletir.

items.example: Well, that could have gone better. Nobody laughed at my joke.
items.exampleTr: Eh, daha iyi geçebilirdi. Esprime kimse gülmedi.
items.simple: A soft way to say: that went badly.
dialogue: A: How was the presentation?
B: That could have gone better. My laptop died halfway through.
items.note: Kötü giden bir şeyden sonra kendini tiye alan kuru ifade.

items.example: Getting here was a bit of a nightmare, the roads were blocked.
items.exampleTr: Buraya gelmek tam bir kabustu, yollar kapalıydı.
items.simple: Very hard or very annoying, but you say it softly.
dialogue: A: How was the move?
B: A bit of a nightmare, honestly. The van never showed up.
items.note: 'a bit of a' kötü şeyi yumuşatır: a bit of a mess, a bit of a problem.

items.en: leave a lot to be desired
items.tr: çok eksiği olmak, pek tatmin edici olmamak
items.example: The service in that place leaves a lot to be desired.
items.exampleTr: O mekandaki hizmetin çok eksiği var.
items.simple: It is not good. It should be much better.
dialogue: A: Did you like the new café?
B: The coffee's great, but the service does leave a lot to be desired.
items.note: Kibar ama net eleştiri; hizmet, yemek, iş kalitesi için.

items.example: It's lovely, but it's a bit on the pricey side.
items.exampleTr: Çok güzel ama biraz pahalıca.
items.simple: It costs a little too much money.
dialogue: A: What did you think of the flat?
B: Nice area, but it's on the pricey side.
items.note: 'on the ... side' kalıbı yumuşatır: on the small side, on the late side.

items.tr: daha iyi günlerim olmuştu, pek iyi sayılmam
items.example: I've had better days, to be honest. My car broke down this morning.
items.exampleTr: Açıkçası daha iyi günlerim olmuştu. Bu sabah arabam bozuldu.
items.simple: A soft way to say: today is a bad day.
dialogue: A: You okay? You look shattered.
B: I've had better days. The baby was up all night.
items.note: 'Nasılsın?' sorusuna dürüst ama dramatik olmayan cevap.

items.example: This homemade pizza is not half bad!
items.exampleTr: Bu ev yapımı pizza hiç fena değil!
items.simple: It is quite good, better than you thought.
dialogue: A: So? What do you think of my curry?
B: Not half bad, actually. Is there any more?
items.note: Daha çok İngiliz İngilizcesi; aslında övgüdür.

items.example: "Was the party loud?" "You could say that. The police turned up."
items.exampleTr: "Parti gürültülü müydü?" "Öyle de denebilir. Polis geldi."
items.simple: Yes, and really much more than that.
dialogue: A: Was the exam hard?
B: You could say that. Half the class left in tears.
items.note: Kuru mizahla 'evet, hem de fazlasıyla' demek.

items.example: Let's just say the date didn't end well.
items.exampleTr: Şöyle söyleyeyim, buluşma pek iyi bitmedi.
items.simple: You hint at something bad without telling every detail.
dialogue: A: How did your parents take the news?
B: Let's just say they weren't thrilled.
items.note: Ayrıntıya girmeden kötü bir şeyi ima etmek için.

items.example: I could be wrong, but isn't the shop closed on Sundays?
items.exampleTr: Yanılıyor olabilirim ama dükkan pazar günleri kapalı değil mi?
items.simple: You are not fully sure, so you say it softly.
dialogue: A: The deadline's next Friday.
B: I could be wrong, but I think it's this Friday.
items.note: Birini kibarca düzeltmenin en yaygın yolu.

items.en: That's one way of looking at it
items.tr: bu da bir bakış açısı (pek katılmıyorum)
items.example: "Getting fired is a fresh start." "That's one way of looking at it."
items.exampleTr: "Kovulmak yeni bir başlangıçtır." "Bu da bir bakış açısı."
items.simple: You don't really agree, but you say it nicely.
dialogue: A: Missing the flight means an extra day of holiday!
B: Well, that's one way of looking at it.
items.note: Kibar ama hafif alaycı itiraz.

items.example: I'm not sure I'd agree. He's always been fair to me.
items.exampleTr: Pek katıldığımı söyleyemem. Bana hep adil davrandı.
items.simple: A gentle way to say: I don't agree.
dialogue: A: The new boss is useless.
B: I'm not sure I'd agree. Give her a chance.
items.note: 'I disagree' demekten çok daha yumuşak.

items.en: I hear what you're saying, but
items.example: I hear what you're saying, but we just don't have the budget.
items.exampleTr: Ne demek istediğini anlıyorum ama bütçemiz yok.
items.simple: I understand you, but I still think something different.
dialogue: A: We should hire two more people.
B: I hear what you're saying, but who's going to pay for them?
items.note: İş yerinde kibar itiraz; ardından asıl görüşün gelir.

items.en: for want of a better word
items.tr: daha iyi bir kelime bulamadığım için
items.example: He's, for want of a better word, a bit intense.
items.exampleTr: Daha iyi bir kelime bulamıyorum ama biraz yoğun biri.
items.simple: You use a word, but you know it is not the perfect word.
dialogue: A: How would you describe her new boyfriend?
B: He's... quirky, for want of a better word.
items.note: Tam oturmayan bir kelimeyi kullanırken araya eklenir.

items.example: The new system's faster, but it's not without its problems.
items.exampleTr: Yeni sistem daha hızlı ama sorunsuz da değil.
items.simple: It is good, but it has some bad parts too.
dialogue: A: Do you like working from home?
B: Mostly, yeah. It's not without its problems, though.
items.note: Çifte olumsuzla hafifletme: 'birkaç sorunu var' demenin kibar yolu.

items.example: The app's a bit rough around the edges, but it works.
items.exampleTr: Uygulama biraz ham ama çalışıyor.
items.simple: Mostly good, but not finished or smooth yet.
dialogue: A: What do you make of the new guy?
B: He's rough around the edges, but he's a hard worker.
items.note: İşler için de insanlar için de: kaba görünen ama iyi biri.

items.example: "Another slice of cake?" "I wouldn't say no."
items.exampleTr: "Bir dilim daha pasta?" "Hayır demem."
items.simple: A shy, polite way to say: yes, please.
dialogue: A: Fancy a cup of tea?
B: Ooh, I wouldn't say no.
items.note: İngilizcede 'evet' demenin alçakgönüllü yolu.

items.example: There's a slight problem: I've locked the keys in the car.
items.exampleTr: Ufak bir sorun var: anahtarları arabanın içinde kilitledim.
items.simple: You say small problem, but it is really a big one.
dialogue: A: Is everything ready for the party?
B: There's a slight problem. The cake is on the floor.
items.note: Kötü haberi yumuşatmak için; çoğu zaman komik etki yaratır.

items.en: I see it a bit differently
items.example: I see it a bit differently. I think the price is the real issue.
items.exampleTr: Ben biraz farklı görüyorum. Bence asıl sorun fiyat.
items.simple: A kind way to say you have another idea.
dialogue: A: The problem is clearly the marketing.
B: I see it a bit differently, actually.
items.note: Toplantıda karşı görüşü çatışmasız sunmak için.

items.example: Correct me if I'm wrong, but didn't you say you'd be here at nine?
items.exampleTr: Yanılıyorsam düzelt ama dokuzda burada olacağını söylememiş miydin?
items.simple: You think you are right, but you ask in a polite way.
dialogue: A: I never said I'd help with the move.
B: Correct me if I'm wrong, but you literally said 'count me in'.
items.note: Çoğu zaman aslında haklı olduğunu ima eder.

items.example: Ordering pizza? It's not the worst idea.
items.exampleTr: Pizza söylemek mi? Fena fikir değil.
items.simple: A soft way to say: that idea is quite good.
dialogue: A: What if we leave early and beat the traffic?
B: It's not the worst idea.
items.note: Övgüyü olumsuzla yumuşatmak, tipik İngiliz tarzı.

items.example: I'm a little concerned that we haven't heard back from them.
items.exampleTr: Onlardan hâlâ haber alamamış olmamız beni biraz endişelendiriyor.
items.simple: You are worried, but you say it calmly.
dialogue: A: The client hasn't replied all week.
B: Yeah, I'm a little concerned that they've lost interest.
items.note: İş yerinde kaygıyı panik yaratmadan dile getirmek için.

items.example: Karaoke's not really my thing, but I'll come and watch.
items.exampleTr: Karaoke pek bana göre değil ama gelip izlerim.
items.simple: You don't like it much, but you say it kindly.
dialogue: A: Want to come to the salsa class?
B: Thanks, but dancing's not really my thing.
items.note: 'Nefret ederim' demeden kibarca geri çevirmek.

items.en: I'm not sure that's quite right
items.tr: bunun tam doğru olduğundan emin değilim
items.example: I'm not sure that's quite right. I think we paid more than that.
items.exampleTr: Bunun tam doğru olduğundan emin değilim. Sanırım daha fazla ödedik.
items.simple: A polite way to say: I think that is wrong.
dialogue: A: So the trip cost us about two hundred quid.
B: I'm not sure that's quite right. Check the receipts.
items.note: 'You're wrong' demenin çok daha kibar hali.
